plan: To prioritize capital preservation, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) to zero.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets approximately 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation and minimizing drawdown. It significantly reduces overall portfolio risk by eliminating leveraged positions and maintaining a cash buffer.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet concentration limits and free up capital.
Reduce exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to small, manageable percentages.
Initiate a new position in NOW at 4%, leveraging a strong scanner setup.
This approach balances broad index exposure with quality tech and a small amount of leverage.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for approximately 2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing a high-quality new long setup.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to comply with the single-name concentration limit.
Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to lean into high-beta sectors.
Initiate a new position in NOW at 6%, capitalizing on a strong scanner setup.
This strategy uses leverage and concentration to target higher growth, with strict stop discipline.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets approximately 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases leverage and concentration, which amplifies both potential upside and drawdown. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this approach can lead to substantial losses quickly without strict stop discipline.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) to zero to reduce volatility.

income.read: This income plan targets approximately 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income from covered-call ETFs, but distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
